notes: kb/Work PB552 (wave 1031 C). 'When the THROUGH phrase is specified: a) ... the value of literal-2 shall be less than the value of literal-3. b) when literal-2 is of class alphanumeric or national, and the runtime collating sequence is known, the value of literal-2 shall be less than the value of literal-3.' (cite.py --check OK). DataBinder.CheckRangesAscending asks every THROUGH pair after the IN alphabet-name-1 phrase resolves: a) algebraically (a numeric conditional variable, or two numeric literals on a numeric-edited one), b) through the ONE ConditionValueOrder SR27 b) reads — the IN alphabet, else the PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE, else native — skipping a LOCALE sequence (SR26 NOTE: unknown). 'Known' is docs/CONFORMANCE.md D-RANGE-KNOWN (GnuCOBOL 3.2 checks neither arm; IBM Enterprise COBOL 6.4 requires literal-1 < literal-2 for every class). Re-probed on this build: 5 THRU 1, 5 THRU 5, 1 THRU 3, 9 THRU 7 (second pair), 9.5 THRU 1.5, "Z" THRU "A" native, "A" THRU "M" under a reversed PCS, "D" THRU "P" IN a reversed alphabet, N"ZZ" THRU N"AA", and 10 THRU 5 on a PIC ZZ9 subject each draw COBOL2961; 1 THRU 5, "Z" THRU "A" IN the reversed alphabet and "Z" THRU "A" IN a LOCALE alphabet compile (the last raises EC-RANGE-INVALID at run time).
